llm-apis.name: Google Gemini API
llm-apis.description: Frontier multimodal models on a permanent free tier — Flash and Flash-Lite families only since April 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,500 requests/day on Flash, 1,000/day on Flash-Lite; 250K TPM
llm-apis.notes: Free-tier prompts are used to improve Google products outside the EU/UK/EEA. Pro models left the free tier in April 2026.

llm-apis.name: Groq Cloud
llm-apis.description: Open-weight models at 300+ tokens/sec on LPU hardware, with the most generous request-per-day allowance of any free tier.
llm-apis.notes: The 200K tokens/day ceiling usually binds before the request count does. Llama models were removed from the free plan in 2026.

llm-apis.name: OpenRouter Free Models
llm-apis.description: One OpenAI-compatible key fronting 19+ `:free` models across providers — the best way to A/B models without multiple signups.
llm-apis.free_limit: 50 requests/day (1,000/day after a one-time $10 credit purchase)
llm-apis.notes: The `:free` roster rotates monthly. Upstream providers frequently return 429s on free variants.

llm-apis.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
llm-apis.description: Serverless inference that runs inside a Worker — no egress cost, no cold-start management, free daily budget.
llm-apis.notes: Budget is denominated in Neurons, not tokens — per-model conversion varies, so budget by testing one call.

llm-apis.name: GitHub Models
llm-apis.description: Frontier and open models behind a GitHub PAT — the lowest-friction free tier if you already have a GitHub account.
llm-apis.free_limit: 150-1,000 requests/day depending on tier and model
llm-apis.notes: Intended for prototyping, not production traffic. Rate limits are per-model.

llm-apis.name: Mistral La Plateforme (Experiment)
llm-apis.description: European-hosted Mistral family with a free Experiment mode worth roughly $10/month of credits, no card required.
llm-apis.free_limit: ~$10/month of credits in Experiment mode (about 1B tokens/month on small models)
llm-apis.notes: Experiment mode trains on your prompts by default. The 2 RPM limit makes it a batch/offline worker, not an interactive backend.

llm-apis.name: NVIDIA NIM API Catalog
llm-apis.description: Free hosted endpoints for NVIDIA-curated open models (Nemotron, Llama, DeepSeek), built for prototyping.
llm-apis.free_limit: 1,000 API credits (26,000 total requests) on signup
llm-apis.notes: Credits are one-time and not refilled; some models are marked as evaluation-use only.

llm-apis.name: Z.ai GLM Flash Models
llm-apis.description: GLM-4.x Flash models served free of charge, popular as a drop-in for reasoning and coding agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unmetered access to GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash
llm-apis.notes: Flash tiers are free but rate-limited during peak hours in Asia.

llm-apis.name: Cohere Trial Keys
llm-apis.description: Every Cohere model including Command A and the Embed/Rerank family on a free trial key, non-commercial use only.
llm-apis.notes: Trial keys explicitly prohibit production/commercial use — fine for a POC, not for a shipped product.

llm-apis.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
llm-apis.description: One router in front of 18 inference partners, with monthly free credits on any account.
llm-apis.notes: The $0.10/month allowance is genuinely small — treat this as a smoke-test credit, not a workload budget.

llm-apis.name: SambaNova Cloud
llm-apis.description: Very fast hosted open-model inference with a permanent per-model daily token allowance.
llm-apis.notes: Quota is per model, so stacking three models triples your effective daily allowance.

llm-apis.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio
llm-apis.description: Qwen family access with a free per-model token grant — the cleanest route to Qwen3 Coder for free.
llm-apis.free_limit: ~1M free tokens per model, valid 90 days
llm-apis.notes: Grants expire 90 days after activation and do not renew — good for a build sprint, not a standing tier.

llm-apis.name: Google Cloud Vertex AI Free Credits
llm-apis.description: Vertex AI access to Gemini and Model Garden on new-account credits — the enterprise-labelled alternative to AI Studio.
llm-apis.notes: Requires a billing account with a card, so it fails the strictest no-card filter — but the $300 covers a serious prototype.

llm-apis.name: Azure AI Foundry Free Credits
llm-apis.description: Azure-hosted OpenAI, Phi and Llama models with the new Azure free-account credit bundle.
llm-apis.notes: Identity verification with a card is mandatory; 30-day clock makes it a sprint budget.

llm-apis.name: Amazon Bedrock Free Tier
llm-apis.description: Bedrock-hosted Claude, Llama and Titan models on the AWS free tier for new accounts.
llm-apis.free_limit: Trial credits for Nova and select models for new AWS accounts
llm-apis.notes: Card required at signup. Bedrock model access must be requested per model in the console.

llm-apis.name: Baidu Qianfan (ERNIE)
llm-apis.description: ERNIE Speed and ERNIE Lite are permanently free on Baidu's Qianfan console for Chinese-language agents.
llm-apis.free_limit: ERNIE Speed and Lite free of charge; others on per-token billing
llm-apis.notes: Requires a mainland-China verified phone number for full access.

llm-apis.name: SiliconFlow
llm-apis.description: Chinese inference host that keeps a rotating set of open models free to call, including embedding and rerank models.
llm-apis.free_limit: Rotating set of free models (Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek small variants)
llm-apis.notes: Free model list changes without notice; the reranker and embedding models are the durable part.

llm-apis.name: Chutes.ai
llm-apis.description: Decentralised open-model inference with a community tier that costs nothing for low-volume agent calls.
llm-apis.free_limit: Community tier: quota-limited free requests across 100+ open models
llm-apis.notes: Community capacity is best-effort; expect queueing at peak. Fine for batch, risky for user-facing agents.

llm-apis.name: Vercel AI Gateway
llm-apis.description: One endpoint in front of every major provider with free monthly included credit and per-request observability.
llm-apis.free_limit: $5/month of included AI credits on the Hobby plan
llm-apis.notes: Also works as a BYOK proxy — you can route your existing free keys through it for logging and failover.

llm-apis.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
llm-apis.description: Free caching, rate-limiting and logging proxy placed in front of any provider, including your own free keys.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free on all plans; caching and analytics included
llm-apis.notes: The single highest-leverage free tool in this list: response caching can stretch a 1,000 req/day quota several-fold.

llm-apis.name: Fireworks AI
llm-apis.description: Fast open-model inference with a small no-card starter credit.
llm-apis.rate_limit: 10 RPM until a payment method is added
llm-apis.notes: The account suspends when the $1 is spent. Treat as a smoke test, not a tier.

llm-apis.name: Cerebras Cloud
llm-apis.description: Wafer-scale inference — still the fastest tokens/sec available — but the permanent free tier ended in July 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: $5 trial credit valid 30 days (card verification required since 2026-07-16)
llm-apis.notes: Downgraded from a no-card permanent free tier to a card-gated 30-day trial. Context is capped at 8K on trial.

llm-apis.name: DeepInfra
llm-apis.description: Cheap open-model inference with a small signup credit and no card requirement for the trial.

llm-apis.name: AI21 Studio
llm-apis.description: Jamba family models with a recurring free allowance aimed at evaluation.
llm-apis.free_limit: $10 in credits every 3 months on the free plan
llm-apis.notes: One of the few providers whose free credit refreshes on a schedule rather than once.

llm-apis.name: Moonshot Kimi API
llm-apis.description: Kimi K2 family with signup credit for long-context Chinese and English workloads.

llm-apis.name: ElevenLabs Free
llm-apis.description: Best-in-class TTS voices with a genuine monthly free character allowance, no card required.
llm-apis.notes: Free-tier output requires attribution and cannot be used commercially.

llm-apis.name: Deepgram
llm-apis.description: Low-latency STT and TTS built for voice agents, with a large one-time credit and no card on signup.
llm-apis.free_limit: $200 one-time credit (roughly 100 hours of Nova-3 transcription)
llm-apis.notes: Credit is one-time; voice agents burn it fast. Pair with a local Whisper fallback.

llm-apis.name: AssemblyAI
llm-apis.description: Speech-to-text plus audio intelligence (summarisation, topic detection) on a no-card starter credit.
llm-apis.free_limit: $50 one-time credit plus rate-limited free transcription

llm-apis.name: Speechmatics
llm-apis.description: Accurate multilingual transcription with a recurring free monthly hour allowance.

llm-apis.name: Google Cloud Speech & TTS
llm-apis.description: Production speech APIs with a standing free monthly allowance for STT and WaveNet/Neural2 voices.
llm-apis.free_limit: 60 min STT + 1M characters TTS per month
llm-apis.notes: The STT/TTS free allowance does not expire, unlike the $300 signup credit — this is one of the best long-term free voice stacks.

llm-apis.name: Azure AI Speech
llm-apis.description: Speech-to-text and neural TTS free allowances inside the Azure free account.
llm-apis.free_limit: 5 hours STT + 500K characters TTS per month

llm-apis.name: Stability AI
llm-apis.description: Stable Diffusion and Stable Audio via API, with a small recurring monthly credit grant.

llm-apis.name: Pollinations.AI
llm-apis.description: Completely keyless text and image generation API — the fastest possible zero-signup smoke test.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unmetered with fair-use rate limits; no API key at all
llm-apis.notes: No SLA and no guarantee of model availability — perfect for demos, unsuitable for production.

llm-apis.name: Leonardo.Ai API
llm-apis.description: Image generation API with a daily free token allowance tied to a free account.

llm-apis.name: Voyage AI
llm-apis.description: High-quality embeddings and rerankers with an unusually large free token grant for RAG prototypes.
llm-apis.free_limit: 200M free tokens across embedding and rerank models
llm-apis.notes: The 3 RPM limit is the real constraint — fine for indexing a corpus offline, painful for live retrieval.

llm-apis.name: Jina AI Embeddings & Reranker
llm-apis.description: Multilingual embeddings, reranker and reader APIs with a large free token allowance on one key.

llm-apis.name: Mistral Codestral
llm-apis.description: Code-specialised completions and fill-in-the-middle model inside the Mistral free Experiment tier.
llm-apis.free_limit: Included in the Mistral free-tier monthly credit

llm-apis.name: Bhashini (ULCA)
llm-apis.description: India's national language platform — free STT, TTS, translation and OCR APIs for 22 scheduled languages.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for developers via the Bhashini API program
llm-apis.notes: Requires registration approval and a pipeline configuration — the signup is heavier than a typical vendor, but the API is genuinely free.

llm-apis.name: Sarvam AI
llm-apis.description: Indian-language LLMs (Sarvam-M), speech and translation APIs with signup credits for Indian developers.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free credits on signup; usage-based afterwards
llm-apis.notes: Indic-language models are the differentiator; English performance is below frontier tiers.

llm-apis.name: Ollama
llm-apis.description: The default way to run open models locally — one command to pull, serve and expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
llm-apis.free_limit: Unlimited; limited only by your GPU/RAM
llm-apis.notes: No rate limit and no data leaving your machine — the correct answer to 'what is the truly free LLM API'.

llm-apis.name: llama.cpp
llm-apis.description: Portable C/C++ inference engine that runs GGUF-quantised models on CPU, GPU or Apple Silicon.

llm-apis.name: LM Studio
llm-apis.description: Desktop GUI for local models with a one-click local server and built-in model discovery.
llm-apis.free_limit: Free for personal and work use

llm-apis.name: vLLM
llm-apis.description: High-throughput serving engine with PagedAttention — the standard for self-hosted production inference.

llm-apis.name: Jan
llm-apis.description: Open-source offline ChatGPT alternative that can also expose a local OpenAI-compatible API.

llm-apis.name: GPT4All
llm-apis.description: Consumer desktop app for running local models on modest hardware, with Python bindings for agents.

llm-apis.name: MLX LM
llm-apis.description: Apple-silicon-optimised inference and fine-tuning library — the fastest local option on a Mac.

llm-apis.name: LocalAI
llm-apis.description: Drop-in OpenAI API replacement that also speaks image, audio and embedding endpoints on modest hardware.

llm-apis.name: KoboldCpp
llm-apis.description: Single-binary llama.cpp wrapper with a built-in web UI and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

llm-apis.name: llamafile
llm-apis.description: Single-file executable that bundles a model and a server — portable agent runtimes with zero install.

llm-apis.name: Text Generation WebUI
llm-apis.description: Feature-rich local web UI with OpenAI-compatible API, extensions and multi-model loading.

llm-apis.name: faster-whisper
llm-apis.description: CTranslate2 reimplementation of Whisper that transcribes locally far faster than the reference build.

llm-apis.name: Piper TTS
llm-apis.description: Fast, small neural TTS that runs on a Raspberry Pi — the free voice layer for offline agents.

llm-apis.name: Sentence Transformers
llm-apis.description: The standard library for local embeddings and reranking — 15K+ models, no API key, no quota.

llm-apis.name: FastEmbed
llm-apis.description: Lightweight ONNX embedding library — CPU-friendly local vectors that pair directly with Qdrant.

llm-apis.name: WebLLM
llm-apis.description: Runs quantised LLMs in the browser on WebGPU — zero server, zero cost, zero data egress.
llm-apis.notes: First load downloads 1-2GB of weights into the browser cache — design for that or you will lose users.

llm-apis.name: Transformers.js
llm-apis.description: Hugging Face pipelines running in the browser or Node via ONNX runtime, with WebGPU acceleration.

llm-apis.name: wllama
llm-apis.description: llama.cpp compiled to WebAssembly with WASM SIMD and threads — GGUF models straight in the browser.

llm-apis.name: OpenAI API
llm-apis.description: No standing free tier. Data-sharing evaluation tokens are the only free path.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — no signup credits; $5 prepay minimum for API access
llm-apis.notes: Unless your org is eligible for the data-sharing token grant, treat OpenAI as paid-only.

llm-apis.name: Anthropic Claude API
llm-apis.description: No public free API tier; the OSS program grants Claude Max to qualifying maintainers instead.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — paid API only. OSS maintainer program gives a Claude Max seat
llm-apis.notes: Free chat on claude.ai is separate from API access — there is no free API key.

llm-apis.name: xAI Grok API
llm-apis.description: No documented free tier; console access requires prepaid credits.

llm-apis.name: DeepSeek API
llm-apis.description: Extremely cheap per-token pricing, but no standing free tier and no signup grant since 2026.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — top-up required (cheapest paid tokens on the market)
llm-apis.notes: DeepSeek weights are open — run V4-Flash locally for free rather than paying the API.

llm-apis.name: Together AI
llm-apis.description: 200+ open models, but the signup trial credit was retired; a $5 minimum purchase is required.

llm-apis.name: Perplexity API (Sonar)
llm-apis.description: Search-grounded Sonar models are paid API only; the free consumer app is not API access.
llm-apis.free_limit: None — Pro subscribers get $5/month of API credit
llm-apis.notes: Tavily, Exa and Brave all have free search tiers — see the MCP list for agent-ready alternatives.

mcp-servers.name: Filesystem
mcp-servers.description: Secure local file operations with configurable allow-listed directories — the reference server every local agent starts with.
mcp-servers.notes: Always pass an explicit allow-listed root. Running it on `/` gives an agent write access to your whole machine.

mcp-servers.name: Fetch
mcp-servers.description: Fetches a URL and converts it to clean markdown for the model, with robots.txt respect and chunked reading.

mcp-servers.name: Git
mcp-servers.description: Read, search and diff a local git repository — history-aware agents without shelling out to raw git.

mcp-servers.name: Memory (Knowledge Graph)
mcp-servers.description: Persistent knowledge-graph memory stored as local JSON — gives an agent recall across sessions for free.
mcp-servers.notes: Pair with a free vector store (Qdrant or Chroma) when the graph grows past a few thousand entities.

mcp-servers.name: Sequential Thinking
mcp-servers.description: Structured step-by-step reasoning with revision and branching — measurably improves multi-step agent plans.

mcp-servers.name: Time
mcp-servers.description: Time and timezone conversion grounded in the host clock — stops agents hallucinating dates.

mcp-servers.name: Everything (Test Server)
mcp-servers.description: Reference server exercising every MCP primitive — the fastest way to test a new client or transport.

mcp-servers.name: GitHub MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Repo automation, PRs, issues, code search and CI workflows — the most-starred MCP server in the ecosystem.
mcp-servers.notes: A hosted remote variant is available at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ if you would rather not run Docker.

mcp-servers.name: Playwright MCP
mcp-servers.description: Browser automation over accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots — deterministic agent browsing in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
mcp-servers.notes: Accessibility-tree snapshots use far fewer tokens than screenshot-based browser agents.

mcp-servers.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
mcp-servers.description: Drives a real Chrome instance for performance traces, console errors and network inspection.

mcp-servers.name: Notion MCP
mcp-servers.description: Reads and writes Notion pages and databases — the cleanest way to give an agent a knowledge base you already maintain.
mcp-servers.notes: Remember to share the specific pages with the integration — a token alone grants nothing.

mcp-servers.name: Sentry MCP
mcp-servers.description: Pulls issues, stack traces and traces into the prompt so an agent can triage production errors.

mcp-servers.name: Supabase MCP
mcp-servers.description: Postgres schema, migrations, edge functions and logs through one authenticated server.
mcp-servers.notes: Start with --read-only; agents granted DDL rights will eventually drop something you wanted.

mcp-servers.name: MongoDB MCP
mcp-servers.description: Query, aggregate and inspect collections, including Atlas administration.

mcp-servers.name: Redis MCP
mcp-servers.description: Key-value access, data structure operations and vector set queries against Redis or Upstash.

mcp-servers.name: Cloudflare MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Fifteen-plus specialised servers for Workers, R2, D1, DNS, logs and Workers AI.
mcp-servers.notes: Each Cloudflare product ships its own server; pick the observability or bindings one rather than enabling all of them.

mcp-servers.name: Vercel MCP
mcp-servers.description: Deployments, build logs, environment variables and project configuration.

mcp-servers.name: AWS MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Official suite covering S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, CloudWatch and 20+ other services.
mcp-servers.notes: Scope IAM to a read-only role before letting an agent near your account.

mcp-servers.name: Azure MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Natural-language management of Azure resources with Entra ID authentication.

mcp-servers.name: Google Cloud MCP Servers
mcp-servers.description: Managed MCP endpoints for Cloud Run, BigQuery, Spanner and gcloud workflows.
mcp-servers.notes: Google has renamed and reorganised these packages several times in 2026 — confirm the current package name on the docs page before copying the install line.

mcp-servers.name: Docker MCP Gateway
mcp-servers.description: Container management plus a gateway that catalogs and proxies hundreds of other MCP servers.

mcp-servers.name: Kubernetes MCP
mcp-servers.description: kubectl-style cluster operations — inspect pods, apply manifests and read logs.
mcp-servers.notes: Point it at a non-production context. An agent with cluster-admin is a very efficient way to delete a namespace.

mcp-servers.name: Terraform MCP
mcp-servers.description: Provider and module registry lookups plus plan/apply assistance for infrastructure as code.

mcp-servers.name: Grafana MCP
mcp-servers.description: Query dashboards, Loki logs and Prometheus metrics from inside the agent loop.

mcp-servers.name: Elasticsearch MCP
mcp-servers.description: Search indices and run aggregations; works against Elastic Cloud or self-hosted.

mcp-servers.name: Stripe MCP
mcp-servers.description: Read customers, invoices and subscriptions, and create payment links from a prompt.
mcp-servers.notes: Use a restricted key in test mode. --tools=all grants write access to live objects if the key allows it.

mcp-servers.name: Figma MCP
mcp-servers.description: Pulls design tokens, layout and component structure out of Figma files into the editor.
mcp-servers.notes: Figma also ships a first-party Dev Mode server on localhost:3845 for desktop app users.

mcp-servers.name: Linear MCP
mcp-servers.description: Create, search and update issues and projects in Linear from the agent loop.

mcp-servers.name: Atlassian MCP
mcp-servers.description: Jira issues and Confluence pages — the enterprise ticketing counterpart to Linear.

mcp-servers.name: Slack MCP
mcp-servers.description: Read channels and post messages — the archived reference server's maintained successor.
mcp-servers.notes: The original Slack reference server was archived in 2026 and now lives in modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived.

mcp-servers.name: Airtable MCP
mcp-servers.description: Read and write Airtable bases — a spreadsheet-shaped backend for agent prototypes.

mcp-servers.name: Google Workspace MCP
mcp-servers.description: Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs and Sheets through a single OAuth'd server.

mcp-servers.name: Zapier MCP
mcp-servers.description: Bridges an agent to 8,000+ app actions without writing per-service integrations.
mcp-servers.notes: Free plan limits how many actions you can expose at once.

mcp-servers.name: n8n MCP
mcp-servers.description: Gives an agent the full n8n node catalogue so it can build and edit workflows.
mcp-servers.auth_type: n8n API key (optional, for live control)

mcp-servers.name: Browserbase MCP
mcp-servers.description: Cloud browser sessions with stealth mode, proxies and session replay for agents.

mcp-servers.name: Apify Actors MCP
mcp-servers.description: Runs any of Apify's 5,000+ scrapers as an agent tool, including the free-tier actors.

mcp-servers.name: ElevenLabs MCP
mcp-servers.description: Text-to-speech generation and voice management inside the agent loop.

mcp-servers.name: Hugging Face MCP
mcp-servers.description: Searches models, datasets and Spaces, and can call Gradio apps as tools.

mcp-servers.name: Qdrant MCP
mcp-servers.description: Stores and retrieves memories in a Qdrant collection — vector memory as a tool, in about four lines of config.
mcp-servers.notes: Pairs with Qdrant's free 1GB cluster, so long-term agent memory costs nothing to start.

mcp-servers.name: Chroma MCP
mcp-servers.description: Local or cloud Chroma collections exposed as MCP tools for RAG and memory.

mcp-servers.name: Neo4j MCP
mcp-servers.description: Cypher queries and graph-schema inspection against AuraDB Free or self-hosted Neo4j.

mcp-servers.name: Postgres MCP Pro
mcp-servers.description: Read-only-safe Postgres access with index tuning and health checks — the maintained replacement for the archived reference server.
mcp-servers.notes: The original @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres reference server was archived in 2025 — many guides still tell you to install it.

mcp-servers.name: SQLite MCP
mcp-servers.description: Query and inspect a local SQLite file, including business-intelligence style summaries.
mcp-servers.notes: Archived but still functional and still the simplest SQLite option. Community forks exist if you need active maintenance.

mcp-servers.name: MySQL MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Read-only-by-default MySQL queries and schema inspection.

mcp-servers.name: Context7
mcp-servers.description: Version-pinned, up-to-date documentation for thousands of libraries — the single highest-value server for coding agents.
mcp-servers.notes: Works without a key at low volume; an API key raises the rate limit. The most-installed MCP server on npm.

mcp-servers.name: Firecrawl MCP
mcp-servers.description: Crawls, scrapes and extracts structured data from sites, returning clean markdown for the model.

mcp-servers.name: Exa MCP
mcp-servers.description: Semantic web search tuned for agents, with deep-research and company-research modes.

mcp-servers.name: Tavily MCP
mcp-servers.description: Search, extract and map endpoints purpose-built for LLM grounding, with a genuinely usable free tier.

mcp-servers.name: Brave Search MCP
mcp-servers.description: Independent web and local search index with a free API tier — no Google/Bing dependency.
mcp-servers.notes: Brave's free tier is rate-limited to roughly one query per second and requires a card for verification.

mcp-servers.name: DeepWiki MCP
mcp-servers.description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository and get answers grounded in its actual code and wiki.

mcp-servers.name: Ref MCP
mcp-servers.description: Token-efficient documentation search across technical sites, alternative to Context7.

mcp-servers.name: DuckDuckGo MCP
mcp-servers.description: Keyless web search and safe text fetching — zero signup, which is rare in search tooling.
mcp-servers.notes: Rate-limited by DuckDuckGo itself; fine for occasional lookups, not for bulk crawling.

mcp-servers.name: Wikipedia MCP
mcp-servers.description: Wikipedia search, article retrieval and section-level summaries.

mcp-servers.name: YouTube MCP
mcp-servers.description: Fetches video transcripts by URL so agents can reason over talks and tutorials.

mcp-servers.name: Obsidian MCP
mcp-servers.description: Read and write notes in a local Obsidian vault — a personal knowledge base as agent memory.

mcp-servers.name: FastMCP
mcp-servers.description: Pythonic framework and CLI for building MCP servers in about ten lines, with a built-in dev inspector.
mcp-servers.notes: If you are writing your own server, start here. It also has `fastmcp dev` for interactive testing.

mcp-servers.name: OpenAPI MCP Server
mcp-servers.description: Turns any OpenAPI/Swagger spec into MCP tools — the fastest path to exposing an existing REST API.

mcp-servers.name: AntV Chart MCP
mcp-servers.description: Generates charts and dashboards (25+ chart types) as images from natural language data.

mcp-servers.name: Puppeteer (Archived)
mcp-servers.description: The original browser-automation reference server. Superseded by Playwright MCP.
mcp-servers.notes: Still installs and works, but receives no fixes. Use @playwright/mcp for anything new.

mcp-servers.name: Google Drive (Archived)
mcp-servers.description: Searches and reads Google Drive files. Superseded by community Workspace servers.
mcp-servers.notes: Archived in 2025. The community google_workspace_mcp server covers this and more.

mcp-servers.name: Slack (Archived Reference)
mcp-servers.description: The original Slack channel-management reference server, now unmaintained.
mcp-servers.notes: Listed so you can recognise it when a tutorial tells you to install it. Use the Zencoder fork instead.

mcp-servers.name: Brave Search (Archived Reference)
mcp-servers.description: Archived reference search server, replaced by Brave's own first-party server.
mcp-servers.notes: Install @brave/brave-search-mcp-server instead.

agent-tools.name: Cursor
agent-tools.description: AI-first code editor with whole-project awareness, tab completion and a multi-file agent.
agent-tools.free_limit: Hobby plan: limited agent requests + 2,000 tab completions/month
agent-tools.notes: Free tier is an evaluation budget, not a workflow. Pair it with Gemini CLI or Cline for the heavy lifting.

agent-tools.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
agent-tools.description: Agentic editor from Cognition — the Windsurf/Cascade lineage, renamed after the 2026 acquisition.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free plan: unlimited tab completion, quota-limited Cascade agent sessions
agent-tools.notes: windsurf.com now redirects to devin.ai. Tab completion is unlimited on every plan, including free — the agent quota is what runs out.

agent-tools.name: GitHub Copilot Free
agent-tools.description: Copilot's genuinely free tier inside VS Code, JetBrains and the GitHub web editor.
agent-tools.free_limit: 2,000 completions + 50 chat/agent requests per month
agent-tools.notes: Requires any GitHub account, including free. Best free choice if you already live in VS Code.

agent-tools.name: Zed
agent-tools.description: Rust-native, GPU-accelerated editor with a free built-in AI tier and bring-your-own-key support.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free AI tier included; unlimited use with your own API keys

agent-tools.name: Kiro
agent-tools.description: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE — writes requirements and design docs before it writes code.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free tier with monthly agentic-interaction quota

agent-tools.name: Trae
agent-tools.description: ByteDance's AI IDE with a free tier built around frontier models and an agent mode.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free plan with monthly premium-model requests
agent-tools.notes: Review the data-retention policy before using it on proprietary code.

agent-tools.name: Amp (Sourcegraph)
agent-tools.description: Frontier agent from Sourcegraph with a free-forever plan, then pay-as-you-go with no subscription required.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free plan with a monthly ad-supported allowance; BYOK option

agent-tools.name: OpenCode
agent-tools.description: Open-source terminal coding agent with a client/server architecture and provider-agnostic model routing.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free software — you bring a model key (free tiers work fine)

agent-tools.name: Kilo Code
agent-tools.description: Open-source VS Code agent with a large free model allocation before you need your own key.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free credits on signup for Anthropic/Gemini models; unlimited with BYOK

agent-tools.name: Gemini CLI
agent-tools.description: Google's open-source terminal agent with the most generous free quota of any first-party CLI.
agent-tools.free_limit: 1,000 requests/day with a personal Google account (60 RPM)
agent-tools.notes: Also ships a free Gemini Code Assist VS Code extension on the same account. The best $0 coding agent in 2026.

agent-tools.name: Qwen Code
agent-tools.description: Qwen's fork of Gemini CLI wired to Qwen3-Coder, with a large free daily request allowance via OAuth.
agent-tools.free_limit: ~2,000 requests/day via Qwen OAuth
agent-tools.notes: Strong on large refactors thanks to Qwen3-Coder's context window. The 2,000/day figure is subject to change.

agent-tools.name: Aider
agent-tools.description: Terminal pair-programmer that commits every change to git and maps your repo into the model's context.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free software — works with any free LLM API key

agent-tools.name: Cline
agent-tools.description: Autonomous coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal, with human approval at every step.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key (including free tiers)
agent-tools.notes: The most flexible free setup: point it at Gemini or Groq free tiers and a full agent costs nothing.

agent-tools.name: Roo Code
agent-tools.description: Cline fork with custom modes (architect, debugger, tester) and an orchestrator mode for multi-step work.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

agent-tools.name: Continue
agent-tools.description: Open-source Copilot alternative for VS Code and JetBrains with customisable model routing.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free software; connect Ollama for genuinely unlimited local use

agent-tools.name: OpenHands
agent-tools.description: Open-source software engineering agent (formerly OpenDevin) that runs in a sandboxed container.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free software; hosted version has limited free credits

agent-tools.name: Goose
agent-tools.description: Block's local-first agent that can extend itself by writing its own MCP extensions.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

agent-tools.name: Crush
agent-tools.description: Charm's glamorous terminal agent with MCP support, LSP awareness and session management.
agent-tools.free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

agent-tools.name: LangGraph
agent-tools.description: Stateful, graph-based agent orchestration with durable execution, human-in-the-loop and time travel.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT). LangGraph Platform has a free developer tier
agent-tools.notes: Choose this over raw LangChain when your agent needs to pause, resume or survive a crash mid-run.

agent-tools.name: LangChain
agent-tools.description: The widest integration ecosystem in the space — 600+ tools, loaders and vector store connectors.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT); no account required

agent-tools.name: LlamaIndex
agent-tools.description: Data framework for RAG: ingestion, chunking, indexing and query engines over your own documents.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT); LlamaCloud has a limited free tier

agent-tools.name: CrewAI
agent-tools.description: Role-based multi-agent crews with delegation, sequential and hierarchical process modes.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)

agent-tools.name: AG2 (AutoGen)
agent-tools.description: Microsoft-originated multi-agent conversation framework: agents that talk to each other until the task is done.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
agent-tools.description: Small, provider-agnostic agent SDK: handoffs, guardrails, sessions and tracing in a few hundred lines.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT); works with any provider, not just OpenAI
agent-tools.notes: Despite the name, it is vendor-neutral — point it at Gemini or Groq and it works unchanged.

agent-tools.name: Google Agent Development Kit
agent-tools.description: Google's agent framework with a built-in dev UI, evaluation harness and A2A protocol support.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: Pydantic AI
agent-tools.description: Type-safe agent framework from the Pydantic team — validated structured outputs and dependency injection.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)

agent-tools.name: smolagents
agent-tools.description: Hugging Face's minimal agent library — code-writing agents in under 1,000 lines of core logic.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: Agno
agent-tools.description: High-performance multi-modal agent framework with built-in memory, knowledge and reasoning tools.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MPL 2.0)

agent-tools.name: DSPy
agent-tools.description: Programs language models instead of prompting them — optimisers compile prompts against a metric.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)

agent-tools.name: Haystack
agent-tools.description: Production RAG and agent pipelines from deepset, with strong evaluation and deployment tooling.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: Letta
agent-tools.description: Stateful agents with long-term memory that manage their own context window (formerly MemGPT).
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0); free cloud sandbox available

agent-tools.name: Semantic Kernel
agent-tools.description: Microsoft's enterprise agent SDK for Python, .NET and Java with planners and process framework.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)

agent-tools.name: Mastra
agent-tools.description: TypeScript agent framework with workflows, evals, RAG and local dev playground.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: Vercel AI SDK
agent-tools.description: The standard TypeScript toolkit for streaming UI plus agents, with unified provider interfaces.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: LiteLLM
agent-tools.description: One OpenAI-shaped interface over 100+ providers, with a proxy that adds budgets, keys and tracing.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)
agent-tools.notes: The cleanest way to stack several free tiers behind one endpoint and fail over automatically when one 429s.

agent-tools.name: n8n
agent-tools.description: Node-based automation with native AI agent nodes, MCP trigger and hundreds of integrations.
agent-tools.free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition is free forever (fair-code licence)
agent-tools.notes: Running the Docker image on a free-tier VM is the cheapest credible production agent host in this list.

agent-tools.name: Dify
agent-tools.description: LLMOps platform for building chat agents, workflows and RAG apps with a visual editor and API output.
agent-tools.free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition free; cloud sandbox free tier

agent-tools.name: Langflow
agent-tools.description: Visual drag-and-drop builder that compiles to LangChain-based flows and exposes each as an API.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (MIT)

agent-tools.name: Flowise
agent-tools.description: Low-code LLM orchestration with agent flows, tools and embeddable chat widgets.
agent-tools.free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

agent-tools.name: Activepieces
agent-tools.description: Open-source Zapier alternative with AI pieces and MCP support, MIT-licensed rather than fair-code.
agent-tools.free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition free (MIT)

free-tiers.name: Vercel
free-tiers.description: Static and serverless hosting with preview deployments per branch and AI Gateway included.
free-tiers.notes: Hobby is explicitly non-commercial. Fine for a side project, against ToS for a paid product.

free-tiers.name: Netlify
free-tiers.description: Static hosting, edge functions and form handling with per-branch deploy previews.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare Pages
free-tiers.description: Unlimited-bandwidth static hosting that pairs with Workers, D1 and R2 on the same free account.
free-tiers.notes: The best free host for this site's own architecture: static output, no egress billing, global CDN.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare Workers
free-tiers.description: V8-isolate serverless functions with cron triggers and durable objects, plus a free Workers AI binding.
free-tiers.notes: The free tier's 10ms CPU limit is generous for API orchestration and tight for anything doing real compute.

free-tiers.name: GitHub Pages
free-tiers.description: Static hosting straight from a repository, with a custom domain and HTTPS included.

free-tiers.name: Render
free-tiers.description: Container and web-service hosting with managed Postgres and cron jobs.
free-tiers.free_limit: 750 instance-hours/mo; services spin down after 15 min idle
free-tiers.notes: The 15-minute spin-down makes cold starts of 30-60s. Fine for demos, painful for a live agent endpoint.

free-tiers.name: Railway
free-tiers.description: Fast deploys from a repo or Dockerfile with databases attached, billed by usage.
free-tiers.free_limit: Trial credits on signup; $5/mo Hobby credit afterwards

free-tiers.name: Fly.io
free-tiers.description: Runs Docker containers close to users with persistent volumes and private networking.
free-tiers.free_limit: Limited free VM allowance for small machines (no managed databases)

free-tiers.name: Koyeb
free-tiers.description: Serverless container platform with a small always-on free instance and GPU options.
free-tiers.free_limit: One free web service instance (0.1 vCPU / 512MB)

free-tiers.name: Deno Deploy
free-tiers.description: Edge TypeScript runtime with KV storage, queues and cron built in — no build step.

free-tiers.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
free-tiers.description: The only major cloud with a permanently free ARM VM generous enough to self-host several services.
free-tiers.free_limit: 4 ARM cores + 24GB RAM, 200GB storage, 10TB egress/mo, forever
free-tiers.notes: Capacity in popular regions is often exhausted — retry or pick another home region. Card required for verification but not charged.

free-tiers.name: AWS Free Tier
free-tiers.description: Twelve months of t4g.small, Lambda allowances and 5GB S3, plus always-free Lambda and DynamoDB caps.
free-tiers.free_limit: 12-month credits for new accounts; perpetual Lambda/DynamoDB allowances

free-tiers.name: Google Cloud Free Tier
free-tiers.description: e2-micro VM, Cloud Run and Firestore allowances, plus the $300 new-account credit.
free-tiers.free_limit: Always-free e2-micro VM + Cloud Run/Speech/BigQuery monthly quotas

free-tiers.name: Hugging Face Spaces
free-tiers.description: Free CPU containers for hosting Gradio or Docker demos, with permanent public URLs.
free-tiers.free_limit: 2 vCPU / 16GB RAM free CPU Spaces (sleep after inactivity on some configs)
free-tiers.notes: Best free way to put a public demo of your agent in front of people.

free-tiers.name: Google Colab
free-tiers.description: Free hosted Jupyter with a T4 GPU — the cheapest path to fine-tuning or running a large model.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free GPU sessions (T4), subject to availability and session limits
free-tiers.notes: Free GPU availability is not guaranteed at peak times and sessions die after idle periods — not a deploy target.

free-tiers.name: Kaggle Notebooks
free-tiers.description: Free GPU/TPU notebooks with 30 hours of weekly GPU quota and persistent datasets.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30 GPU hours/week (P100 or T4x2), 20 TPU hours/week

free-tiers.name: Modal
free-tiers.description: Serverless Python with GPU-per-second billing — good for embedding jobs and batch inference.
free-tiers.free_limit: $30/month of included compute on the free plan
free-tiers.notes: $30/month covers a lot of embedding generation; it does not cover sustained GPU inference.

free-tiers.name: E2B
free-tiers.description: Sandboxed cloud VMs built for agent code execution, with filesystem and process control.

free-tiers.name: Val Town
free-tiers.description: Write and deploy TypeScript functions in the browser with cron, SQLite and secrets included.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free tier with 100K daily function runs

free-tiers.name: Supabase
free-tiers.description: Postgres with auth, storage, realtime and pgvector in one free project — the default agent backend.
free-tiers.notes: Free projects pause after 7 days of inactivity. Set up a weekly keep-alive ping or accept the cold start.

free-tiers.name: Neon
free-tiers.description: Serverless Postgres with copy-on-write branching — a database branch per feature or per agent run.

free-tiers.name: Turso
free-tiers.description: Edge SQLite with embedded replicas — sub-millisecond reads next to your function, plus native vector search.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare D1
free-tiers.description: SQLite at the edge, bound directly to Workers with no connection pooling to manage.

free-tiers.name: CockroachDB Basic
free-tiers.description: Distributed SQL with automatic replication across regions and standard Postgres wire protocol.

free-tiers.name: MongoDB Atlas
free-tiers.description: Managed document database with a permanent M0 cluster, including Atlas Vector Search.
free-tiers.notes: Card verification is required even for M0 in most regions now — the one free database that usually asks.

free-tiers.name: Firebase Firestore
free-tiers.description: Realtime document database with offline sync and client SDKs for every platform.

free-tiers.name: Aiven
free-tiers.description: Managed Postgres, MySQL, Valkey and OpenSearch on a single always-free plan.
free-tiers.free_limit: One 1GB managed service (Postgres, MySQL, Valkey or OpenSearch)

free-tiers.name: Convex
free-tiers.description: Reactive backend with TypeScript queries, mutations, scheduled functions and vector search.

free-tiers.name: Upstash Redis
free-tiers.description: Serverless Redis with per-request pricing and a REST API — no connection limit problems from serverless functions.

free-tiers.name: PocketBase
free-tiers.description: Single-binary backend with SQLite, auth, file storage, realtime and an admin UI — self-host anywhere.

free-tiers.name: Cloudflare R2
free-tiers.description: S3-compatible object storage with zero egress fees — the reason to store agent artefacts here.
free-tiers.free_limit: 10GB storage, 1M Class A ops/mo, free egress

free-tiers.name: Backblaze B2
free-tiers.description: Cheap S3-compatible object storage with free egress through Cloudflare's bandwidth alliance.

free-tiers.name: Qdrant Cloud
free-tiers.description: The best free vector tier: a real cluster with payload filtering, no card required.
free-tiers.free_limit: 1GB cluster free forever (0.5 vCPU, 1GB RAM, 4GB disk)
free-tiers.notes: 1GB holds roughly 250K vectors at 384 dimensions — enough for a serious RAG prototype.

free-tiers.name: Pinecone Starter
free-tiers.description: Fully managed vector database with the least operational overhead of any option here.
free-tiers.free_limit: 2GB storage, 2M write units and 1M read units/mo, 5 indexes
free-tiers.notes: Free indexes are pinned to AWS us-east-1 — latency from India or Europe is noticeable.

free-tiers.name: Weaviate Cloud
free-tiers.description: Open-source vector database with hybrid keyword+vector search and built-in vectoriser modules.

free-tiers.name: Zilliz Cloud
free-tiers.description: Managed Milvus with strong performance at scale and a genuine free cluster.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free tier: 5GB storage, 2.5M vector compute units/mo

free-tiers.name: Upstash Vector
free-tiers.description: Serverless vector database over REST — no connection management, pairs with Upstash Redis on one key.

free-tiers.name: Chroma Cloud
free-tiers.description: Managed version of the most developer-friendly embedded vector store, with $5 of starter credit.
free-tiers.free_limit: $5 starter credit; Chroma OSS remains free to self-host
free-tiers.notes: For anything under a few hundred thousand vectors, self-hosted Chroma on the same box as your app is simpler and free.

free-tiers.name: Neo4j AuraDB Free
free-tiers.description: Managed graph database with native vector indexes — a knowledge graph and a vector store in one.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free instance: 200K nodes, 400K relationships, no card required

free-tiers.name: pgvector
free-tiers.description: Postgres extension that turns the database you already run into a vector store — no second system to operate.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (extension; self-hosted or on any Postgres free tier)
free-tiers.notes: Available out of the box on Supabase and Neon free tiers — the pragmatic default for a small agent.

free-tiers.name: LanceDB
free-tiers.description: Embedded vector database on the Lance columnar format — runs in-process, no server, no account.

free-tiers.name: Clerk
free-tiers.description: Drop-in authentication with prebuilt UI components, organisations and webhooks.

free-tiers.name: WorkOS AuthKit
free-tiers.description: Auth with enterprise SSO, SCIM and directory sync built in from day one.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free up to 1M monthly active users on AuthKit
free-tiers.notes: The 1M MAU number makes this the strongest free option if you might later need enterprise SSO.

free-tiers.name: Auth0
free-tiers.description: Mature identity platform with social logins, MFA and rules/extensibility.

free-tiers.name: Logto
free-tiers.description: Open-source auth alternative to Auth0 with a clean developer experience and a free cloud tier.
free-tiers.free_limit: 50,000 MAU on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited

free-tiers.name: Better Auth
free-tiers.description: TypeScript-first authentication library that lives inside your app — no third party in the request path.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (MIT, self-hosted in your own codebase)
free-tiers.notes: For an agent app, a library beats a hosted auth service: no MAU cliff, no extra vendor.

free-tiers.name: Keycloak
free-tiers.description: Red Hat's battle-tested identity server — full OIDC/SAML with self-hosting on a free VM.

free-tiers.name: Upstash QStash
free-tiers.description: HTTP-based message queue and scheduler — the simplest way to add durable background jobs to serverless agents.

free-tiers.name: Inngest
free-tiers.description: Durable workflow engine with steps, retries and fan-out — long-running agents that survive restarts.
free-tiers.notes: The most direct fix for 'my agent died halfway through': each step is checkpointed and retried.

free-tiers.name: Trigger.dev
free-tiers.description: Background jobs as code with long-running tasks, realtime progress and observability.

free-tiers.name: Ably
free-tiers.description: Realtime pub/sub and presence for streaming agent output to a browser.

free-tiers.name: Pusher Channels
free-tiers.description: Managed WebSockets with channels, presence and client events.

free-tiers.name: Novu
free-tiers.description: Notification infrastructure that fans out one event to email, in-app, chat and push channels.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30K events/mo on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited

free-tiers.name: CloudAMQP
free-tiers.description: Managed RabbitMQ on a small always-free instance — proper AMQP when QStash is not enough.

free-tiers.name: Langfuse
free-tiers.description: Open-source LLM tracing, prompt management and evaluation — the default for debugging agent runs.
free-tiers.free_limit: 50K observations/mo on free cloud; self-hosted is unlimited
free-tiers.notes: Self-hosting on the Oracle always-free ARM VM gives you unlimited tracing for $0.

free-tiers.name: Helicone
free-tiers.description: One-line proxy that logs every LLM request with cost, latency and caching.

free-tiers.name: Sentry
free-tiers.description: Error tracking with stack traces, releases, session replay and an official MCP server.

free-tiers.name: Grafana Cloud
free-tiers.description: Metrics, logs and traces with a permanent free tier plus 14-day retention.

free-tiers.name: Axiom
free-tiers.description: Log analytics built for high-cardinality events, with dashboards and alerts.
free-tiers.notes: 0.5TB/month free is unusually large — useful if you log every agent step and tool call.

free-tiers.name: PostHog
free-tiers.description: Product analytics, session replay, feature flags and experiments in one SDK.

free-tiers.name: Better Stack
free-tiers.description: Uptime monitoring, status pages, on-call alerting and log management.
free-tiers.free_limit: 10 monitors at 3-min checks, 1 status page, 3GB logs

free-tiers.name: UptimeRobot
free-tiers.description: Simple external uptime checks with Slack and email alerts — the guardrail for 'is my agent alive'.

free-tiers.name: Plausible Analytics
free-tiers.description: Privacy-first, cookie-free web analytics — no consent banner needed, GDPR-compliant by design.
free-tiers.free_limit: 30-day trial on cloud; self-hosted Community Edition is free forever
free-tiers.notes: This project's own site should self-host Plausible or Umami — a cookie banner would violate the 'no dark patterns' principle.

free-tiers.name: Umami
free-tiers.description: Lightweight, open-source, cookie-free analytics with a simple dashboard.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free (MIT, self-hosted); managed cloud has a small free allowance

free-tiers.name: Resend
free-tiers.description: Transactional email API with React Email templates and good deliverability.

free-tiers.name: Brevo
free-tiers.description: Transactional email plus marketing campaigns and SMS on one generous free plan.

free-tiers.name: Mailtrap
free-tiers.description: Email sandbox for testing plus a small sending allowance — stops agents spamming real inboxes in dev.
free-tiers.free_limit: 1,000 emails/mo sending; free sandbox for testing

free-tiers.name: Algolia
free-tiers.description: Hosted search with typo tolerance, synonyms and instant-search UI libraries.

free-tiers.name: DocSearch
free-tiers.description: Free Algolia-powered documentation search for open-source projects, including crawl and the search UI.
free-tiers.free_limit: Free for open-source and developer documentation
free-tiers.notes: Requires your docs to be public and crawlable — this project's site qualifies.

free-tiers.name: Typesense Cloud
free-tiers.description: Open-source (GPL) search engine with typo tolerance and vector search, self-hostable or managed.
free-tiers.free_limit: Self-hosted is free; cloud offers trial clusters
free-tiers.notes: The managed cloud often lacks a permanent free cluster now — budget to self-host on the free Oracle VM.
